drhp.business: Aries Agro is an agri-input company manufacturing micronutrient fertilizers, plant nutrition products, biostimulants and Plantomycin, along with an expanding equipment division for crop protection and mulching. It sells domestically across 28 states through a dealer network and exports to Australia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Nepal, Philippines, Taiwan, UAE, Sri Lanka, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique, Uzbekistan, Bangladesh, Mauritius and other emerging markets, supported by an overseas branch in Fujairah, UAE.
drhp.end_markets: 28 states across India|Australia|New Zealand|Nigeria|Nepal|Philippines|Taiwan|United Arab Emirates|Sri Lanka|Saudi Arabia|Mozambique|Uzbekistan|Bangladesh|Mauritius
drhp.expansion: During FY 2025-26, Aries Group commissioned a new manufacturing facility at Sayakha, Bharuch (6,000 MT capacity, commenced February 2026), and separately inaugurated its 7th/8th manufacturing facility at Saykha, Gujarat for Boric Acid and Water Soluble products (12 February 2026). Associate company Amarak Chemicals FZC completed relocation of its Sulphur Bentonite manufacturing unit from Fujairah to JAFZA, Dubai (inaugurated 17 January 2026). The Company also inaugurated a relocated manufacturing facility at Lucknow (5 March 2026) and expanded distribution/logistics infrastructure: a new City Office at Vijayawada (2 April 2025), a Bio Products Analysis Laboratory and Plantomycin Microbial Analysis Laboratory at Vijayawada (3 April 2025), an expanded automated warehouse at Nashik (16 June 2025), a Vertical Automatic Stacking System at Hyderabad (12 July 2025), its 30th depot at Siliguri (22 August 2025), and an expanded automated depot with Plantomycin manufacturing licence at Vijayawada (30 November 2025).

litigation.note: No material Orders have been passed by any Authority in respect of any matters with regard to the business of the Company (Board's Report, Item 11).

risks.note: Demand for agricultural inputs is influenced by monsoon conditions, crop acreage, farm incomes and commodity prices; increasing weather variability, including excessive or deficient rainfall and extreme weather events, may affect crop productivity and consequently demand.
Volatility in prices and availability of key raw materials, energy costs, logistics disruptions, foreign exchange movements and geopolitical developments may impact costs and margins.

Increasing competition from organized and unorganized players, changing farmer preferences and evolving distribution channels require continuous innovation, product differentiation and strong market reach.
Changes in Government policies, fertilizer regulations, product registrations, environmental norms and quality standards may affect operations and market dynamics.
Performance depends on attracting and retaining skilled personnel and maintaining robust manufacturing, quality, safety, information-security and internal-control systems.

High probability of Super El-Nino, geopolitical trends from the West Asia war, China's export restrictions on fertilizers, lower farm-gate prices for agri produce and a 94% monsoon projection versus the Long Period Average indicate a subdued and uncertain trend for the agro industry.

Geopolitical uncertainties, global trade disruptions, supply chain constraints, and volatility in ocean freight, crude oil and natural gas prices, foreign exchange rates, and input costs may impact the business.

sk.overview: The agrochemicals (crop protection) industry covers the development, manufacture and distribution of insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and plant growth regulators in Formulations and Technicals form. Per the issuer-commissioned ICRA Report (February 2026), the sector is supported by resilient Indian agriculture (healthy reservoir levels, robust crop production sustaining rural demand), a global 'China+1' shift favouring Indian chemical manufacturing, and sustained government fiscal support to agriculture and manufacturing.
sk.schemes: Make in India|Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme (incl. bulk drugs / KSM / API, total outlay Rs 6,940 crore FY2021-FY2030)|Bharat Vistar multilingual AI advisory platform (Union Budget)|Coconut Promotion Scheme and cashew-cocoa initiatives|PM Gati Shakti, National Logistics Policy, Dedicated …
sk.structure: The DRHP frames agrochemicals within globally dispersed supply chains for raw materials, intermediates and finished products, subject to tariff and trade-flow sensitivity. India is positioned as a beneficiary of 'China+1'/'Europe+1' localisation, with import substitution supported by PLI schemes …

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- FY 2026-27 outlook is expected to be subdued and uncertain due to high probability of Super El-Nino, geopolitical trends from the West Asia war, China's fertilizer export restrictions, lower farm-gate prices for agri produce, and a 94% monsoon projection versus the Long Period Average
- International sales saw temporary moderation due to the relocation of associate company Amarak Chemicals FZC's manufacturing facility from Fujairah to JAFZA and short-term geopolitical factors in the Middle East, with management expecting to regain momentum
- Domestic subsidiaries Mirabelle Agro Manufacturing and Aries Agro Equipments showed strong growth momentum, reinforcing the Company's expanding footprint
- Growing farmer awareness of balanced crop nutrition, soil health improvement and the need for enhanced agricultural productivity are cited as opportunities for growth
- Company plans to deepen market penetration, strengthen bulk and institutional business segments, and explore domestic and international market opportunities
- Annual booking programme for FY 2026-27 conducted online secured orders worth Rs.1,084.40 crore from 1,788 dealers across 22 states, expected to be lifted during FY 2026-27

Associate company Amarak Chemicals FZC completed relocation of its Sulphur Bentonite manufacturing unit from Fujairah to JAFZA, Dubai (inaugurated 17 January 2026). The Company also inaugurated a relocated manufacturing facility at Lucknow (5 March 2026) and expanded distribution/logistics infrastructure: a new City Office at Vijayawada (2 April 2025), a Bio Products Analysis Laboratory and Plantomycin Microbial Analysis Laboratory at Vijayawada (3 April 2025), an expanded automated warehouse at Nashik (16 June 2025), a Vertical Automatic Stacking System at Hyderabad (12 July 2025), its 30th depot at Siliguri (22 August 2025), and an expanded automated depot with Plantomycin manufacturing licence at Vijayawada (30 November 2025).

- technology: import-substitution manufacturing capability for water-soluble fertilizers — evidence: Aries HD range sales grew from Rs.920.89 lakhs (FY24) to Rs.3,866.56 lakhs (FY26), reducing dependence on China imports

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Demand for agricultural inputs is influenced by monsoon conditions, crop acreage, farm incomes and commodity prices; increasing weather variability, including excessive or deficient rainfall and extreme weather events, may affect crop productivity and consequently demand.
- Volatility in prices and availability of key raw materials, energy costs, logistics disruptions, foreign exchange movements and geopolitical developments may impact costs and margins.
- Increasing competition from organized and unorganized players, changing farmer preferences and evolving distribution channels require continuous innovation, product differentiation and strong market reach.
- Changes in Government policies, fertilizer regulations, product registrations, environmental norms and quality standards may affect operations and market dynamics.
- Performance depends on attracting and retaining skilled personnel and maintaining robust manufacturing, quality, safety, information-security and internal-control systems.
- High probability of Super El-Nino, geopolitical trends from the West Asia war, China's export restrictions on fertilizers, lower farm-gate prices for agri produce and a 94% monsoon projection versus the Long Period Average indicate a subdued and uncertain trend for the agro industry.
- Geopolitical uncertainties, global trade disruptions, supply chain constraints, and volatility in ocean freight, crude oil and natural gas prices, foreign exchange rates, and input costs may impact the business.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Reduce dependence on imported raw materials through 'Make in India' / backward integration, shifting global sourcing share from 18% (FY25) to 13% (FY26) of total raw material requirement
- Diversify supplier base across multiple geographies (China, Brazil, Turkey, UAE) to reduce reliance on any single region for cost efficiency, material specialisation and supply dependability
- Expand global footprint through partnerships, distributor engagement and participation in international exhibitions to grow export volumes and enter new markets
- Automation and backward integration at new factories to enable self-production of critical raw materials
- Promote climate-resilient ('climate proof') products and expand the range of plant protection and agro-equipment products
- Enhance inventory holding at additional locations ahead of season to manage demand-supply volatility
- Continued investment in in-house R&D (DSIR-recognised) focused on crop-specific formulations, hydroponic nutrients, HD formulations, precision agriculture including drone-based applications, bio-stimulants, water-soluble fertilizers, urban gardening, organic inputs and sustainable packaging
